name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Pressure on oil importers such as Egypt, but no emerging-market crisis
state: The Egyptian pound passed 56 per dollar at the central bank on 26 Oct, a record low, and Egypt unexpectedly raised rates by one point to 20% on 29 Oct, citing energy prices (Rio Times). Indonesia has repeatedly intervened for the rupiah this year. No major emerging economy has defaulted, imposed capital controls or lost more than 10% in a month as of 1 Nov.
for_you: Oil-importing emerging economies are under strain from the energy shock. People with ties to Egypt may see further moves in the exchange rate.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month or emergency IMF request

sources.title: Rio Times — Egypt raises interest rates to 20%
TradingView (Reuters) — Indonesia central bank stepping up FX interventions after rupiah hits record low

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
